statement: C0029 asks, for iid Bernoulli sign matrices B_n, for P(s_min(B_n)<=epsilon/sqrt(n))<=epsilon+exp(-Omega(n)) for all epsilon>=0 and large n. Theorem 1.1 of Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney supplies (1+O((log n)^(-1/16)))epsilon+exp(-Omega(n)), so the exact coefficient is not implied by that theorem.

source.quote: where the o(1) term decays as C_xi(log n)^(-1/16)

proof_or_counterexample: Direct comparison of the displayed conjecture and Theorem 1.1; w574's abstract distribution counterexample confirms the logical gap.
independent_reviewer: w578 pending for this sourced row
remaining_gap: No Bernoulli-specific coefficient-one estimate; current openness not fully verified against 2026 literature.

statement: The C0029-A001 assertion that P(sqrt(n) s_min(G_n)<=t)=1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is exact for every finite real Gaussian matrix size n is false.
assumptions: G_1 has a standard real Gaussian entry

source.quote: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t)

proof_or_counterexample: For n=1 the exact CDF is P(|Z|<=t)=2Phi(t)-1, whose right derivative at zero is sqrt(2/pi), whereas 1-exp(-t-t^2/2) has right derivative 1. The latter is the limiting hard-edge CDF, not the n=1 law.
remaining_gap: Does not by itself sharpen the Bernoulli least-singular-value bound.
